news.title: Create while the world keeps moving.
news.summary: Native creation sharing, part checks and safe editor commits reach the next experimental milestone.
paragraphs: A newly saved creature can now travel between the original SPORE games used in our tests. The dedicated game checks its native parts and abilities, and the receiving game loads the same creation under its own local identity.

Editing was tested while another player continued moving and jumping. Cancelling a changed draft preserved the saved creature. A finished creation became a shared version only after the required checks succeeded; unfinished drafts stayed unpublished.

The tests also refused a missing part before importing the creation and caught a changed terrain record before opening the game. The received model and its original test-drive movement were inspected in SPORE.

This completes M08 within the recorded Creature test setup. Sharing still uses development tools and locally approved creations; it is not available as a public campaign feature. The next milestone is preserving progress and recovering safely after server restarts.

news.title: One encounter. Shared results.
news.summary: Combat, feeding and reconnecting now agree across a recorded original-game Creature encounter.
paragraphs: The shared Creature scene has moved beyond movement tests. Two original game clients and a dedicated original-game worker completed a bounded encounter with combat, contested feeding and consistent results.

The session was challenged with delayed and dropped network packets. Reconnecting preserved the recorded result, while stale or wrong-owner updates were rejected. A fresh-session reset also returned to native movement and jumping.

M07 is verified for this specific Creature setup. It does not yet cover the full Creature campaign, all five stages or a public Internet-ready release. Native content and editor transactions are the next foundation.

news.title: Our first steps in a shared world.
news.summary: Two games, one shared scene. Movement, jumping and reconnecting reach an early milestone in the original SPORE.
paragraphs: Two copies of the original SPORE joined the same Creature stage scene, run by a dedicated instance of the game. Each player controls a separate character; movement and jumps were compared in recorded tests.
The launcher also lets players join this scene with a private invitation. A test of closing the game and reconnecting returned to the same character without creating a duplicate.

This is an experimental milestone, limited to a test scene with living creatures. It is not yet a playable co-op campaign. The observed issues with death, respawning and reconnecting after a respawn are part of the next step.

news.title: One reward. Counted once.
news.summary: A DNA gain recorded in the original game was applied to a test instance without triggering a second reward.
paragraphs: To share a world, connected games need to agree on the outcome of each action. A Creature stage combat scenario verified that a gain of 8.75 DNA points could be applied without awarding it twice.

These tests lay the groundwork for sharing outcomes between players while preserving the original game's rules. Safeguards were also tested to prevent the receiving instance from producing conflicting progress.
The result is limited to this specific scenario. Other abilities, inventories, complete encounters and progression through the full campaign still need development and testing.

news.title: The world continues after you leave.
news.summary: In testing, a dedicated game instance continued its actions after the player's game and launcher were closed.
paragraphs: A persistent universe should not depend on a player staying connected. A dedicated instance of the original SPORE continued the planned actions in a test scene after the player's game and launcher were closed.
A save of that scene was then reloaded with the same characters. Tests also checked that two development instances and their saves remained separate.

This foundation is not yet a hosting solution ready for players. The tests currently require rendered game windows that remain open and are not minimized. Preserving all progress, handling restarts and connecting over the Internet still need work.

releases.title: Clearer shared-world checks
changes: Check the saved world and companion files before opening SPORE to join.
Name a missing or different world file so the mismatch can be identified.
Keep existing saves in place while checking that players and hosts use matching development builds.
releases.note: Development version. Creation sharing remains a developer test path; no public multiplayer download yet.

releases.title: An invitation to join
changes: Join the experimental scene from the launcher with a private invitation.
Return with the same player identity after disconnecting.
See the connection status directly on the home screen.
releases.note: Development version. The full multiplayer campaign and Internet hosting are still in development.

releases.title: More reliable test sessions
changes: Keep the selected test server when its status refreshes.
Let start and stop requests finish after the launcher closes.
Fix a logging issue that could prevent a later launch.
releases.note: These improvements apply to the development tools.

releases.title: Your game, your resolution
changes: Choose fullscreen or windowed mode and a resolution in Settings.
Keep your display preferences between launches.
releases.note: The settings are implemented; not every display combination has been verified in the game.

roadmap.title: Keep progress through restarts
roadmap.description: M09: preserve native checkpoints and creation versions, reconnect safely and recover interrupted changes after a server restart.

roadmap.title: Explore apart. Meet again.
roadmap.description: Connect separately simulated locations in one canonical universe, with safe transfers and shared consequences.

roadmap.title: From Cell to Space
roadmap.description: Cover all five stages, their editors and transitions, with independent progression for each player.

roadmap.title: Make it ready for players
roadmap.description: Simplify installation and Internet hosting, then test the complete campaign before a public release.
